canonical_title: Second Variety and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A career-spanning volume of PKD's short fiction anchored by 'Second Variety,' his 1953 tale of self-replicating war machines that learn to counterfeit humanity, later filmed as Screamers.
page_summary:
Second Variety and Other Classic Stories takes its title from Dick's 1953 story about autonomous killing machines on a devastated battlefield who evolve new models designed to pass as wounded soldiers, children, and refugees. The premise fuses his lifelong preoccupations: the android that imitates the human well enough to destroy it, and the impossibility of knowing who around you is real. It later became the film Screamers (1995).

As one of the volumes drawn from Dick's collected short fiction, the book gathers work from the 1950s, the decade in which he produced stories at a furious pace for the science-fiction magazines. The recurring figures are here: the ordinary man caught in a machinery of empire and war, the betrayal that arrives from the least expected quarter, the ground of reality giving way.

The collection is a useful entry point to Dick's short work because the title story shows, in miniature, the moral engine that drives the later novels: empathy as the one test that distinguishes the human, and the terror of a world engineered to defeat that test.
